# google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config

Configs of a publisher model.

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
See [Provider Versions](../guides/provider_versions.html.markdown) for more details on beta resources.

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Publisher Model Config Global Full


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config" "claude_global" {
  provider = google-beta

  location  = "global"
  publisher = "anthropic"
  model     = "claude-fable-5-1"

  logging_config {
    enabled             = true
    sampling_rate       = 0.1
    error_sampling_rate = 1

    bigquery_destination {
      output_uri = "bq://${data.google_project.project.project_id}.${google_bigquery_dataset.claude_global.dataset_id}"
    }

    enable_otel_logging = true
  }

  data_sharing_enabled_provider = "ANTHROPIC"
}

resource "google_bigquery_dataset" "claude_global" {
  provider = google-beta

  dataset_id                 = "example_dataset"
  friendly_name              = "genai_log"
  location                   = "US"
  delete_contents_on_destroy = true
}

data "google_project" "project" {
  provider = google-beta
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `location` -
  (Required)
  The model's location.

* `publisher` -
  (Required)
  The model provider's name.

* `model` -
  (Required)
  The model's name.


* `logging_config` -
  (Optional)
  The prediction request/response logging config.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_logging_config).

* `data_sharing_enabled_provider` -
  (Optional)
  The model provider (publisher) for which the customer has enabled data sharing.
  For publisher models that are configured to require data sharing, a prediction request is only allowed when the model's publisher matches this provider.
  Otherwise, the request is rejected.
  Default value is `MODEL_PROVIDER_UNSPECIFIED`.
  Possible values are: `MODEL_PROVIDER_UNSPECIFIED`, `ANTHROPIC`.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.



<a name="nested_logging_config"></a>The `logging_config` block supports:

* `enabled` -
  (Optional)
  If logging is enabled or not.

* `sampling_rate` -
  (Optional)
  Percentage of requests to be logged, expressed as a fraction in range(0,1].

* `error_sampling_rate` -
  (Optional)
  Percentage of failed requests to be logged, expressed as a fraction in range [0,1].
  Only non-transient errors will be logged (currently `500/Internal errors`).

* `bigquery_destination` -
  (Optional)
  BigQuery table for logging.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_logging_config_bigquery_destination).

* `request_response_logging_schema_version` -
  (Output)
  The schema version used in creating the BigQuery table for the request response logging.
  The versions are "v1" and "v2". The current default version is "v1".

* `enable_otel_logging` -
  (Optional)
  This field is used for large models. If true, in addition to the original large model logs,
  logs will be converted in OTel schema format, and saved in otel_log column. Default value is false.


<a name="nested_logging_config_bigquery_destination"></a>The `bigquery_destination` block supports:

* `output_uri` -
  (Required)
  BigQuery URI to a project or table, up to 2000 characters long.
  If only given a project, a new dataset will be created with name `publishers_<publisher>_models_<model>`
  where will be made BigQuery-dataset-name compatible (e.g. most special characters will become underscores).
  If no table name is given, a new table will be created with name `request_response_logging`.
  When the full table reference is specified, the dataset must exist and table must not exist.
  If the endpoint is global, the dataset have to be specified.
  Accepted forms: BigQuery path. For example: `bq://projectId`, `bq://projectId.bqDatasetId` or `bq://projectId.bqDatasetId.bqTableId`.

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

## Import


PublisherModelConfig can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/publishers/{{publisher}}/models/{{model}}/publisherModelConfig`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}`
* `{{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import PublisherModelConfig using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    publisher = "<-required value->"
    model = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import PublisherModelConfig using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/publishers/{{publisher}}/models/{{model}}/publisherModelConfig"
  to = google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), PublisherModelConfig can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/publishers/{{publisher}}/models/{{model}}/publisherModelConfig
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default {{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}
```
